study.title: Modulation of functional activity and connectivity by acupuncture in patients with Alzheimer disease as measured by resting-state fMRI
study.study_design: Single-block experimental design with pre- and post-acupuncture resting-state fMRI in AD patients and healthy controls
study.population: 14 AD patients and 14 age-, gender- and education-matched healthy controls (HCs); all right-handed
study.inclusion_criteria: AD patients recruited from Xuanwu Hospital, Beijing, China; HCs recruited from local community by advertisements; all right-handed; HCs should have had no neurological diseases and no cognitive dysfunction; neuropsychological assessments based on DSM-4th Edition criteria for dementia and NINCDS-ADRDA
study.exclusion_criteria: Subjects whose head motion exceeded 2.5 mm in translation or 2.5 degrees in rotation in any direction were excluded
study.source_location: Abstract, p.1; Materials and methods > Subjects, p.2-3; Imaging preprocess, p.4

extraction_notes.note: No sham acupuncture control condition was used. The authors explicitly acknowledge this as a limitation: 'it will be more helpful to set a control state to compare real-needle acupuncture with sham acupuncture.' All comparisons are within-subject (pre vs post) in AD patients only, or between AD and HC groups.
No sensory, deqi, or interoceptive response measures were reported. No instruments such as MASS, VAS for needle sensation, or similar scales were administered or mentioned.
extraction_notes.source_location: Throughout the paper; not reported in any section

extraction_notes.note: No expectancy, credibility, blinding success, or allocation guessing measures were reported or assessed.

extraction_notes.note: The statistical method for comparing pre vs post ALFF in AD patients is described as 'paired-samples t test analysis' in one place and 'independent-samples t-test' in another for the FC z-values. The text states: 'First, we extracted the z values for the pre-acupuncture and post-acupuncture stages for the AD patients. Then, an independent-samples t-test was run for each of the ROIs (pre-acupuncture versus post-acupuncture).' This is potentially an inconsistency since a paired-samples t-test would be expected for within-subject comparison. Extracted as stated in the paper.
extraction_notes.source_location: Statistical analysis, p.5; Results > ALFF changes, p.6

extraction_notes.note: The exact p-values for the individual paired comparisons shown in Fig 3 for IFG_R, Hippocampus_R, and MCC (decreased ALFF after acupuncture) are not reported in text or table; only significance symbols (* and **) in the figure are described. The narrative text states these showed 'decreased ALFF after acupuncture' without explicit p-values for each region.
extraction_notes.source_location: Results > ALFF changes, p.6; Fig 3, p.6

extraction_notes.note: The figure legend for Fig 3 states ** represents significantly changed ALFF (P<0.05) and * represents slightly changed (P>0.05). However, the narrative text states 'Fig 3 shows the significantly increased ALFF in the left postcentral gyrus in the AD patients when comparing the post-acupuncture with the pre-acupuncture stage (P<0.05)' and also that 'The right SFG also showed an increased ALFF after acupuncture although the statistical result did not reach the significance threshold.' This suggests Postcentral_L = ** and SFG_R = *, but it is ambiguous whether the decrease in IFG_R, Hippocampus_R, and MCC are significant (P<0.05 **) or not.
extraction_notes.source_location: Fig 3 caption, p.6; Results text, p.6

extraction_notes.note: The AVLT correlations with ALFF and FC values are described as using AVLT-delayed recall in the figure labels (Fig 5 and Fig 6), but the results section refers to 'AVLT scores' generally. The specific AVLT sub-score (delayed recall) is inferred from figure axis labels.
extraction_notes.source_location: Fig 5, p.8; Fig 6, p.9; Results > Correlations, p.7

extraction_notes.note: The paper describes 'increased ALFF' in several regions in AD at baseline as potentially compensatory, but it is unclear from the methods whether the ALFF values reported in Fig 3 bar graphs are from the baseline or from some normalized measure. The bar graph y-axis label is 'ALFF values' for both pre and post acupuncture bars.

Table 2 footnote abbreviates 'IFG, inferior temporal gyrus' but IFG stands for inferior frontal gyrus throughout the rest of the paper. This appears to be a typographic error in the table footnote. Extracted as IFG = inferior frontal gyrus following consistent usage throughout the paper.
Needle manipulation details (e.g., twirling, lifting-thrusting, rotation speed, number of manipulations, whether deqi was elicited or confirmed) are not described.

It is unclear whether the HC group also received acupuncture. The study design section implies acupuncture was performed in a single session for all participants, but the focus of the post-acupuncture analysis is only on AD patients. HC post-acupuncture data are not analyzed or reported.
extraction_notes.source_location: Data acquisition, p.3; Statistical analysis, p.4

extraction_notes.note: Number of participants excluded due to excessive head motion is not reported. The motion threshold criterion is stated but the actual exclusions (if any) are not described.

The paper states 'mean FDR' as a covariate in the between-group ALFF analysis. The meaning of 'mean FDR' as a covariate (rather than a correction method) is unusual and unclear; it may refer to mean framewise displacement ratio or another motion summary metric.
extraction_notes.source_location: Statistical analysis, p.4; Table 2 footnote, p.6
